fronts.caption: NELL AND THE HAT. A Speaker composograph: the hat is hers, the head under it was unavailable for the sitting.
A SPEAKER COMPOSOGRAPH. No camera went down to the boiler room. The figure was posed in our art room from the description; the flue is the flue.
The boiler room of the Long Island City courthouse, where the record was burned.
VALVES GO UP. The glass shop at Newark, six alarms.
Beardstown. Twelve hundred men on the bank, six inches below the crown.
About 9,400 marching, the Exchange's operators among them.
SHE STAYED. The Division's men pack up at Port Washington; Sixteen-Ten does not.

features.caption: AT THE PLATE. Drawn from the wire description, the Speaker's man being unable to see past the pillar.
FOR THE FALL. The wide hats go out with the summer; the cloche stays.

dramas.byline: Posed by Speaker players, from a true account

stills.caption: "That voice! But Harold said he was at the lodge!"
"Who taught you to listen at walls, Mabel Doyle?"
"Keep the set. I have heard enough for one lifetime."

pictures.caption: Nell's last week. Twenty summers up Steinway Street, and the children of the route bring carrots.
Above the El. A rooftop, the first cool evening, and something good on the portable.
Sunday at the board. The exchange answers, holiday or no.
The bridge at lamp time, from the Queens side.
